newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel declines against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel declines against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened mildly against the dollar on Monday but rose against the basket of key foreign currencies in mixed trading, dealers said.
"Trading was mixed today, with the shekel trading slightly lower against the dollar following the rise of the American currency abroad," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"The rise of the dollar against the shekel was minimal and the basket fell to 6.86 percent below the diagonol rate," he said.

The shekel fluctuates in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
"As long as the Bank of Israel keeps the interest rate unchanged the shekel is expected to remain strong," the trader said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2470 shekels against 3.2420 shekels on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6187 shekels against 3.6275 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8006 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7970 on Friday and against the mark at 2.0722 shekels against 2.0980 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2470 shekels.
